source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: The Number of Prorogators, and also the Part of Fortune
source_locator.short_quote: The part of Fortune is ascertained by computing the number of degrees between the Sun and the Moon; and it is placed at an equal number of degrees distant from the ascendant, in the order of the signs.

prerequisites: relative order of the Sun and Moon
calculation_dependencies: relative order of the Sun and Moon for the preserved directional variant

condition.operation: measure the Sun-Moon degree interval and place the Part of Fortune at an equal interval from the Ascendant so the Moon-Part relation matches the Sun-Ascendant relation
condition.sect_statement: the cited main text states the same procedure by day and night
condition.directional_status: unresolved; compare the separate Perugio variant

normalized_rule: In Ashmand's main text, compute the Part of Fortune from the Sun-Moon degree interval and place the point an equal interval from the Ascendant so the Moon's relation to the Part of Fortune corresponds to the Sun's relation to the Ascendant; the text says the same procedure applies by day and night, while the directional footnote variant is preserved separately.
synthesis_notes: This is a traditional astrological point calculation within the cited transmission, not an astronomical measurement or a scientific claim.
review_notes: The candidate records the main-text procedure without selecting a directional winner. The additional Perugio Latin instruction in footnote 144 is represented by a separate candidate and an active chart-changing conflict.
transmission_notes: Ashmand's main text states the relational procedure for day and night; footnote 144 reports an additional Perugio Latin directional variant. The main-text shorthand and the footnote variant are retained without collapsing them. Certainty is confidence in this cited Ashmand/Proclus transmission, not in an autograph of Ptolemy.
